commons.title: Ati Boracay livelihood b.jpg
commons.credit: Alan J. Dacalan for the Department of Agriculture (Philippines)
commons.description: Department of Agriculture Secretary Emmanuel Piñol turns over tools like sprinkler, UV film, spading fork, spade, plastic drums, planting materials, and assorted vegetable seeds to the Ati tribe of Barangay Manoc-manoc in Malay, Aklan on June 27, 2018. The Agriculture chief initially committed PHP2 million in financial support to the indigenous people's and women's groups of Boracay through the Survival Recovery loan program.
commons.editorial_reason: Ati attribution is specific, but the image shows modern aid distribution and ordinary clothing, not visible Ati cultural expression.

commons.title: Ati community in Boracay.jpg
commons.credit: Alan J. Dacalan for the Department of Agriculture (Philippines) edited by LOR
commons.description: Department of Agriculture Secretary Emmanuel Piñol urged the Ati Tribe members of Brgy. Manoc-manoc in Malay, Aklan to turn their 2.1 hectare-ancestral domain into an agri- tourism site to uplift their lives from poverty and provide them access to government interventions' on Wednesday (June 27, 2018) during a meeting  with the agri chief who initially committed Php 2 million financial support to the Indigenous People's (IPs) and women's groups of Boracay via the Survival Recovery (SURE) loaning program
commons.editorial_reason: The caption identifies an Ati community, but the meeting shows ordinary modern clothing and no visible cultural dress, craft, or performance.

commons.title: Ati Outfit.jpg
commons.description: The Ati Tribes were the origin of the Ati-Atihan as a tribute to their pagan gods, all covered in black and dancing in weird steps that are mostly random. Native Aklanons and Jesus devotees would wear similar costumes as profession of faith to their Christian religion
commons.editorial_reason: The Ati-specific caption ties the image to Ati-related festival attire and visibly shows painted/costumed performers.

commons.title: Ati Boracay livelihood.jpg
commons.credit: Alan J. Dacalan for the Department of Agriculture (Philippines)
commons.description: Smiling under the heat of sun, Ati tribe members cultivate the warm sand in Barangay Manoc-manoc in Malay, Aklan in preparation for vegetable seed planting as is one of their livelihood projects assisted by the Department of Agriculture (DA). DA Secretary Emmanuel Piñol visited the poverty-stricken area and initially committed PHP2 million in financial support to the indigenous peoples and women's groups of Boracay through the Survival Recovery (SURE) loan program
commons.editorial_reason: The caption specifically identifies Ati workers, but the image shows ordinary modern clothing and livelihood activity without visible Ati cultural expression.
